titre: Rickets Cured by a Lamp, Three Years Before Vitamin D
accroche: In 1919 Berlin, rachitic children are cured under an ultraviolet lamp. The vitamin D it triggers in their skin would not be identified for three more years.
contenu_vulgarise:
Berlin, winter 1918-1919. Four years of war and blockade have reduced poor children's diets to almost nothing: no milk, little butter, even less cod liver oil. Many grow up with bowed legs, a deformed chest, swollen wrists: rickets, a disease that keeps bones from mineralizing properly. The pediatrician Kurt Huldschinsky, at the Charité hospital, tries something unusual on four of these children: he exposes them, one hour, three times a week, to the radiation of a mercury-vapor lamp, a “höhensonne,” an “artificial alpine sun” originally designed to treat skin tuberculosis.

## A cure before the explanation

Within a few weeks, X-rays of the exposed children show a marked increase in bone mineralization, especially at the ends of the long bones. A comparable group, left untreated, shows almost none. Huldschinsky publishes his first results in 1919 in the Deutsche Medizinische Wochenschrift, then extends them to thirty children in a May 1920 paper: artificial ultraviolet light cures rickets as reliably as cod liver oil, the standard treatment for decades. The news spreads fast across Europe: dozens of clinics install arc lamps for their young patients.

The most striking part is not the cure, it is what nobody yet knows in 1919. Huldschinsky has no idea why a light produces what a fatty food also produces. Cod liver oil has treated rickets since the nineteenth century without anyone knowing which of its components acts. In 1918, the British researcher Edward Mellanby had just shown that it also protects laboratory puppies, proof that a specific nutritional factor is at work, not some general virtue of fat. But a food and a radiation seem, on the face of it, to have nothing in common.

## The missing link, found afterward

The rest unfolds over three years. In 1922, Elmer McCollum's team at Johns Hopkins shows that heated and aerated cod liver oil loses its activity against night blindness, the vitamin A effect, but keeps intact its action against rickets. A distinct factor is therefore at work, which they name vitamin D. At the same time, Alfred Hess and Harry Steenbock independently discover that irradiating certain foods, or even an animal's skin, with ultraviolet light confers this same antirachitic activity. The two threads meet: the light Huldschinsky had aimed at his patients triggers, in their skin, the production of the very substance that cod liver oil delivered to them ready-made.

For three years, then, a treatment worked, was published, reproduced, extended to hundreds of children, without anyone being able to say what it did to the body or why. The story of vitamin D is thus written backward from what one expects of a medical discovery: practice preceded biochemistry, and it was by trying to understand a lamp that two teams ended up isolating a vitamin.

repere.texte: In his May 1920 paper on thirty rachitic children, Huldschinsky reports a marked increase in bone mineralization visible on X-ray after four weeks of ultraviolet exposure, where an unexposed control group shows almost no improvement. The vitamin D that this light triggers in the skin would not be isolated and named until 1922.
repere.source: Holick, M.F., “Resurrection of vitamin D deficiency and rickets,” The Journal of Clinical Investigation, vol. 116, no. 8, 2006, p. 2062-2072

carte.punch: A lamp cured rickets three years before vitamin D was discovered.
carte.idee: In 1919, Kurt Huldschinsky cures rachitic children with an ultraviolet lamp, without knowing why it works. The substance it triggers in their skin, vitamin D, would not be isolated and named until 1922, by a team starting from cod liver oil.

pour_aller_plus_loin.titre: Holick, M.F. (2006), full text, open access (PMC)
pour_aller_plus_loin.note: Retraces the whole history of vitamin D, from cod liver oil to its chemical identification in 1922.

quiz.question: Why did Huldschinsky's treatment work in 1919 without anyone being able to explain why?
choix: Because the lamp's heat disinfected the bones and stopped an infection that caused rickets
Because the exposed children were also, in parallel, given cod liver oil injections
Because ultraviolet light triggers, in the skin, the production of vitamin D, isolated only in 1922
Because exposure to artificial sunlight mainly boosted their appetite and dietary calcium intake
quiz.explication: Ultraviolet light triggers, in the skin, the production of vitamin D, the same factor supplied by cod liver oil. This substance would not be isolated and named until 1922, three years after Huldschinsky's publication.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What was the standard treatment for rickets before ultraviolet lamps appeared?
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Cod liver oil had treated rickets since the nineteenth century, without anyone knowing which of its components acted, long before Huldschinsky tried ultraviolet light.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the British researcher Edward Mellanby show in 1918?
choix: That sunlight plays no role in preventing rickets
That cod liver oil also protects laboratory puppies against rickets
That rickets is a contagious infectious disease
That vitamin D is found only in cow's milk
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Mellanby shows in 1918 that cod liver oil also protects laboratory puppies, proof that a specific nutritional factor is at work, not some general virtue of fat.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does Elmer McCollum's team establish in 1922?
choix: That vitamin A and vitamin D are in fact the same substance
That ultraviolet light destroys all antirachitic activity in cod liver oil
That rickets has no link at all to diet
That heated cod liver oil loses its effect against night blindness but keeps its effect against rickets, revealing a distinct factor named vitamin D
quiz_supplementaire.explication: By isolating a factor that survives heating where the vitamin A factor does not, McCollum's team establishes in 1922 that a distinct substance is at work, which they name vitamin D.
